notes: 5K and Elk Double runners must pick up their bib by 5:00 PM on Friday.
This is a cup-free event — no disposable cups on course. Bring a handheld bottle, hydration vest, or reusable cup.
Our expo is bag-free. Don't forget to Bring Your Own Bag (BYOB)! Reusable bags also available at the merch tent.
Pre-order merch? Pick it up at the merch booth during expo or race day — just show your order confirmation.

courseInfo.heading: 5K Info
courseInfo.aidStations: One aid station near the halfway point (approximately mile 1.5–1.8) with water, electrolytes, and bathrooms. Cup-free — bring your own vessel.
courseInfo.recoveryFood: Post-race recovery food available at the finish line. Stick around for the awards ceremony at 7:00 PM!
courseInfo.strollerPolicy: The 5K course is on paved roads and is stroller- and wheelchair-friendly. Please be mindful of other participants and stay to the right.
courseInfo.dogPolicy: Dogs are not allowed on the course. They're welcome to cheer you on from the finish line!

parkingOptions.name: Ball Fields (Primary Lot)
parkingOptions.details: First lot to fill. Located east of Community Drive near the start and finish lines. Approach via Hwy 7, turn east onto Manford Avenue toward the fairgrounds. Volunteers on-site to direct traffic.

parkingOptions.name: High School & Observatory (Second Lot)
parkingOptions.details: Second lot to fill. Short walk to start/finish lines. Follow volunteer direction from Manford Avenue.

parkingOptions.name: Fairgrounds (Third Lot)
parkingOptions.details: Overflow parking. Please only park in designated areas marked on the event map. Follow volunteer direction.

shuttleDetails.label: Runners line up, last call for gear check

raceMorning.dropOffNote: Approach via S St Vrain Ave (Hwy 7) and turn onto Manford Avenue toward the fairgrounds. Follow crew to the drop-off area, then exit the parking lot back onto Community Drive heading south toward N St Vrain Ave. Please move quickly to keep traffic flowing for other runners.

spectators.notes: We welcome spectators to Rocky Mountain this year! Spectators are welcome at the finish line and may park according to the main parking locations and schedule. The finish line is walking distance from town, which has many shops and restaurants to pass the time until your runner finishes!
warnings: Please only park in designated areas. There should be plenty of parking for everyone. Following this guideline allows us to continue putting on successful events compliant with local authorities.
Once your runner has finished their race, please stay outside of the runner recovery area to avoid crowding.
Finish line drinks, supplies, and the medical tent are there for runners only. Please respect this.

postRace.finishLineInfo: The finish line is on the south shore of Lake Estes near the Stanley Ball Fields. Post-race recovery bags include snacks, bananas, and chocolate milk. Merch tent opens at 8:00 AM. Gear check bags available once the first runner finishes. Course record holders receive a free race entry every year their record stands!

infoSections.heading: Zero Waste
infoSections.body:
Our events take place in and around protected national park landscapes, and we are deeply committed to minimizing waste while preserving the natural beauty of the places we run — without compromising safety, efficiency, or hydration on course.

To achieve this, we've implemented cup-free racing across the series: runners may add a lightweight, foldable reusable cup during registration or bring any personal hydration system that doesn't produce trash. Self-serve aid stations are placed throughout the course with water and electrolytes for quick, efficient refills, allowing athletes to hydrate as needed without waste, congestion, or mess. The system keeps courses clean, stations moving smoothly, and hydration reliable.

infoSections.heading: Awards
infoSections.body:
Place medals will be given to the top 5 male, female, and non-binary runners overall, as well as the Masters 40+ group.

Additionally, the top 5 in each of the following age groups will also receive a place medal: 11 and younger, 12–14, 15–19, 20–24, 25–29, 30–34, 35–39, 40–44, 45–49, 50–54, 55–59, 60–64, 65–69, 70–74, 75 and older. We do not currently offer non-binary age group awards.

There will be finisher medals for everyone who finishes the race.

infoSections.heading: Results & Photos
infoSections.body:
Live results will be hosted online by Laurel. Results are not official until all runners have crossed the finish line and been reviewed by the event director. Questions about placement? Email timing@brooksee.com.

Top finisher but missed the awards ceremony? You can request to have your place medal shipped to you.

New for 2026 — FinisherPix will be at each event to capture your race memories. Photos are available within 24–48 hours post-event. The FinisherPix Photo Pack includes all photos in all digital formats. Search for your photos by last name or bib number.

challengeEvents.intro: Looking to push further? Take on both races in one weekend and earn exclusive finisher swag.

events.name: Elk Double
events.description: The Elk Double is for runners who want to take on two distances in one weekend. Run the 5K on Friday evening and the Half Marathon on Saturday morning. Finishers earn a special Elk Double medal (in addition to each race medal) and one exclusive swag item of their choice. You'll use the same bib for both events.
includes: Race medal and shirt for each event (5K and Half Marathon)
Your choice of one exclusive Elk Double swag item: hat, unisex t-shirt, beach hoodie, or Nalgene bottle
One bib used for both races
events.bibPickup: Pick up your Elk Double bib (used for both races), race shirt, and swag item at the race expo on Friday, July 31 between 12:00 PM and 5:00 PM. If your shirt doesn't fit, exchange it at the finish line after the half marathon on Saturday.
events.medals: Once you've completed the Elk Double, collect your special finisher medal just outside the runner recovery area. A clearly marked table will be waiting for you — show your bib and a volunteer will hand you your Elk Double medal.
events.swag: Your pre-chosen swag item will be ready at the expo. Additional items may be purchased only after your final race to ensure all participants receive their requested item. If you opted out, additional items can be purchased at the end of the second race.

lodging.description: Our official lodging partner, offering exclusive rates for runners, friends, and family near the Expo, Start Line, and Finish Line — plus 24/7 support if plans change.

activities.name: Rocky Mountain National Park
activities.description: All visitors need a park pass to enter — pick one up at the entrance or at recreation.gov. Use the timed entry reservation system to avoid crowds. Visit nps.gov/romo for trail conditions and planning info.

activities.name: Train with Runna
activities.description: Personalized training for your next Vacation Races event. Download now and unlock two free weeks with code VACATIONRUNNA.

activities.name: Race Swag & Merchandise
activities.description: The official race shirt is picked up at expo upon check-in, and your finisher medal is awarded at the finish line. Exclusive race merchandise — beach hoodies, t-shirts, hats, bottles, and more — will be available at expo and near the finish line. Leftover merch will be available in the online store after the event.

activities.name: Personalize Your Medal — iTab
activities.description: Make your medal last forever with an iTab: a custom engraved plate with your name and finishing time that clips onto your medal ribbon. Pre-order before race day and it ships automatically after you finish. Just $15 including postage.

restaurants.name: The Bird's Nest

restaurants.name: Bird & Jim

restaurants.name: Inkwell & Brew

restaurants.name: Estes Park Distilling Co.

items.question: If I can't pick up my bib on Friday at the expo, can I pick it up race morning?
items.answer: Yes, for the Half Marathon only. Morning bib pickup opens at 4:15 AM at the start line. 5K and Elk Double runners must pick up at the Friday expo — no race morning option for those events.

items.question: Can someone else pick up my race packet?
items.answer: Yes, as long as they have a photo of your ID.

items.question: Are dogs, strollers, or wheelchairs allowed on course?
items.answer: Dogs are not permitted on course but are welcome at the finish line. Both the Half Marathon and 5K courses are on paved roads and are stroller- and wheelchair-friendly. Stay to the right and be mindful of other participants.

items.question: This is a cup-free event — what does that mean?
items.answer: There are no disposable cups on course. Bring a handheld bottle, hydration vest, or your Nathan reusable cup (available as a registration add-on). Water and Gnarly Hydrate electrolytes will be available at all aid stations.

items.question: Where should I park on race morning?
items.answer: Three designated lots are near the fairgrounds, all within a short walk to the start and finish lines. Approach via Hwy 7 and turn east onto Manford Avenue — volunteers will direct you. Lots fill in order: Ball Fields first, then High School & Observatory, then Fairgrounds. Arrive by 5:15 AM.

items.question: Do I need a National Park pass to attend the race?
items.answer: The race start and finish area is in Estes Park and does not require a park pass. If you plan to visit Rocky Mountain National Park before or after the race, you'll need a pass and should reserve a timed entry permit at recreation.gov.

items.question: How can I defer or transfer my entry?
items.answer: Deferrals to any Vacation Races Half Marathon or Trailfest are processed on Let's Do This — a 50% admin fee applies. Entry transfers to another participant are available online until the Wednesday before the event or in person at expo. A $30 transfer fee applies to the original runner.

items.question: What happens if the race is cancelled?
items.answer: All registration fees are non-refundable. In the event of a cancellation for emergency reasons (weather, pandemic, etc.), refunds cannot be provided. We offer Refund Protect at registration for qualifying personal circumstances.
